about: Leadership Roadmap wording for each Maxwell DISC style code. Every DISC-driven passage in the booklet comes from the reader's own style entry, so C, CS and CSD (for example) read differently. CSD carries the approved reference booklet's wording (Courtney Stanford V4) verbatim. Codes not listed fall back to their first two letters, then their first letter. Fields: natural_strengths (Profile table) / experience (How Staff May Experience You) / blind_spot (Potential Blind Spot; Snapshot mirror row) / pressure_risk (Pressure Risk; Snapshot risk row) / coaching_adjustment (DISC Coaching Adjustment; Snapshot pattern row) / risk_response (Snapshot risk row, second column) / coaching (Snapshot Coaching Opportunity, both columns) / creates (Integration Summary: 'In a leadership role, this creates ...') / foundation (DISC Connection page: 'a strong foundation in ...', four words) / development (DISC Connection page: 'The development opportunity is to ...') / limit (30-day DISC step: 'where it may limit ...') / focus_move (Roadmap Focus: move from [0] to [1], ..., and [2]) / fly_risk (Flywheel page, after 'The development risk is that ') / plan_focus (30-60-90 Primary Coaching Focus) / plan_60, plan_90 (30-60-90 DISC Component) / success (90-Day Success Indicator, after its fixed first sentence) / fly_ground (Flywheel page: 'a leadership pattern grounded in ...') / signature (Leadership Signature: quality and stretch are the first two named qualities and Observable Behavior rows; trust and momentum fill 'I build trust through ___ and authentic communication' and 'create momentum by pairing ___ with visible support and clear direction').

D.natural_strengths: Decisiveness, directness, urgency, and results-focused drive
D.experience: direct, confident, decisive, and focused on outcomes
D.blind_spot: May move faster than team trust or alignment can support, and may under-invest in relational connection.
D.pressure_risk: May become more forceful, more impatient, or more likely to take over rather than coach.
D.coaching_adjustment: Slow down to align, listen for impact, and coach ownership instead of driving compliance.
D.risk_response: Pause before deciding, invite input, and let others own the next step.
coaching: Move from directing the answer to coaching supervisors to find it.
Ask for their recommendation before giving yours, then hold them to it.
D.creates: clear direction, decisive action, momentum, and a strong drive for results
D.development: channel that drive into shared ownership, so the team moves with you rather than behind you
focus_move: coaching others to own the outcome
D.fly_risk: speed and decisiveness can outrun the team's ownership if you direct more than you coach. Your Flywheel work is to ensure momentum is shared, not just driven.
D.fly_ground: decisive direction, results focus, and a strong sense of urgency
D.plan_60: Move from driving the result to coaching others to own it. Ask before directing.
D.plan_90: Keep the pace without taking over. Stay inclusive and coaching-oriented when urgency rises.
D.success: Your pace remains strong, and staff increasingly bring their own recommendations and own outcomes rather than waiting for your direction.

quality: Decisiveness
You set clear priorities and explain the reasoning behind them.
stretch: Openness
You invite input before deciding and let others own the next step.

DI.natural_strengths: Bold vision, decisiveness, and results-focused drive, supported by enthusiasm, persuasion, and the ability to rally people
DI.experience: bold, inspiring, fast-moving, and energizing, with a clear sense of where the team is headed
DI.blind_spot: May launch more initiatives than the team can finish, and may assume enthusiasm equals commitment.
DI.pressure_risk: May push harder and talk faster, sell the vision instead of listening, or move on before the work is finished.
DI.coaching_adjustment: Pair every new direction with an owner, a timeline, and a follow-up, and let others shape the plan before you sell it.
DI.risk_response: Slow the launch, confirm who owns what, and finish before starting the next thing.
coaching: Move from inspiring the start to coaching supervisors through the finish.
Ask what it will take to complete the work, then hold the follow-up date.
DI.creates: bold direction, contagious energy, fast starts, and a strong push toward new possibilities
DI.development: anchor that momentum in execution, so initiatives are finished as well as launched
focus_move: coaching others to carry the work to completion
DI.fly_risk: momentum can depend on your energy if the plan is not translated into owners and systems. Your Flywheel work is to ensure initiatives are finished, not just launched.
DI.fly_ground: bold vision, decisive direction, and contagious energy
DI.plan_60: Move from selling the vision to coaching others to own the plan. Confirm owner, action, and date.
DI.plan_90: Keep the energy while protecting focus. Finish current commitments before launching new ones.
DI.success: Your energy and vision remain strengths, and staff increasingly carry initiatives through to completion rather than relying on your momentum to keep them moving.

quality: Vision
You describe where the team is going and why it matters.
stretch: Completion
You turn direction into clear owners, actions, and dates.

DC.natural_strengths: Decisiveness, high standards, and results-focused drive, supported by analytical rigor and quality control
DC.experience: direct, demanding, analytical, and focused on getting the right result
DC.blind_spot: May challenge ideas so quickly that people stop offering them, and may prize being right over bringing others along.
DC.pressure_risk: May become more critical, more exacting, or more likely to overrule others with data and authority.
DC.coaching_adjustment: Lead with questions before critique, explain the standard behind the challenge, and recognize progress as well as gaps.
DC.risk_response: Ask before challenging, name what is working, and agree the standard together.
coaching: Move from correcting the work to coaching supervisors to meet the standard.
Ask how they would improve it before you point out what is wrong.
DC.creates: clear direction, rigorous standards, sound decisions, and a strong drive for quality results
DC.development: pair that challenge with alignment, so people own the standard instead of fearing it
focus_move: coaching others to own the standard
DC.fly_risk: high standards delivered as challenge can quiet the team you need to engage. Your Flywheel work is to ensure standards are shared, not just enforced.
DC.fly_ground: decisive direction, rigorous standards, and sound judgment
DC.plan_60: Move from critiquing the work to coaching the standard. Ask before correcting.
DC.plan_90: Hold high standards without shutting down input. Stay curious and coaching-oriented when pressure rises.
DC.success: Your standards remain high, and staff increasingly raise ideas, challenge constructively, and meet the standard without waiting for your correction.

quality: Rigor
You set a clear, high standard and explain the reasoning behind it.
stretch: Open Dialogue
You ask for other views before you challenge or decide.

DS.natural_strengths: Results-focused drive, persistence, and decisiveness, supported by steadiness and dependable follow-through
DS.experience: driven, steady, dependable, and focused on getting the work done
DS.blind_spot: May carry the workload personally and let steady production stand in for visible leadership.
DS.pressure_risk: May put your head down and push harder, take on more yourself, or become impatient with slower progress.
DS.coaching_adjustment: Delegate the work you would normally carry, share the bigger picture, and make your direction visible beyond the task.
DS.risk_response: Step back from the task, name the priority, and hand the next piece of work to someone else.
coaching: Move from producing the results yourself to coaching supervisors to produce them.
Hand off one piece of work each week and coach the handoff instead of taking it back.
DS.creates: reliable results, steady drive, persistent follow-through, and a strong production focus
DS.development: turn that steady production into visible leadership, so the team's output grows beyond what you carry yourself
focus_move: coaching others to carry the load
DS.fly_risk: steady personal production can hide the need for team capacity if you keep carrying the work. Your Flywheel work is to ensure results come from the team, not just from you.
DS.fly_ground: results-focused drive, persistence, and reliable production
DS.plan_60: Move from carrying the work to coaching others to carry it. Delegate before you take it on.
DS.plan_90: Keep your drive while building the team's capacity. Stay visible and strategic when the pace increases.
DS.success: Your drive remains strong, and staff increasingly own the production and results rather than depending on you to carry the heaviest load.

quality: Drive
You keep the work moving and set a steady, results-focused pace.
stretch: Presence
You share the bigger picture so staff see where their work fits.

DIS.natural_strengths: Decisive direction and results-focused drive, supported by relational energy, persuasion, and steady follow-through
DIS.experience: decisive, engaging, adaptable, and able to mobilize people around a goal
DIS.blind_spot: May adapt to every audience so readily that priorities shift, and may rely on personal energy instead of systems.
DIS.pressure_risk: May spread effort across too many people and priorities, or push momentum through personal effort rather than structure.
DIS.coaching_adjustment: Narrow the priorities, build simple systems that hold the pace, and let accountability rest on process as well as relationship.
DIS.risk_response: Narrow the focus, name the one priority, and put a system behind it.
coaching: Move from mobilizing people personally to building systems that keep them moving.
Agree the measure of success with each supervisor and review it on a set rhythm.
DIS.creates: decisive direction, people-mobilizing energy, steady persistence, and broad momentum
DIS.development: focus that adaptability through clear priorities and systems, so momentum holds when you are not in the room
focus_move: coaching others to sustain the pace
DIS.fly_risk: momentum can depend on your presence if priorities shift with every conversation. Your Flywheel work is to ensure the pace is held by systems, not just by energy.
DIS.fly_ground: decisive direction, people-mobilizing energy, and steady persistence
plan_focus: Sustaining Momentum Without You in the Room
DIS.plan_60: Move from mobilizing people to building the systems that keep them accountable. Agree the measures.
DIS.plan_90: Keep your adaptability while holding steady priorities. Stay focused and consistent when demands multiply.
DIS.success: Your ability to mobilize people remains a strength, and staff increasingly sustain momentum through clear priorities and systems rather than your personal energy.

quality: Mobilizing Energy
You rally people around a clear goal and keep them moving.
stretch: Focus
You name the one priority that matters most and hold it.

DIC.natural_strengths: Decisive, strategic direction, supported by relational influence and analytical credibility
DIC.experience: strategic, credible, persuasive, and confident in the direction
DIC.blind_spot: May stay at the level of strategy and influence, assuming a well-reasoned plan will execute itself.
DIC.pressure_risk: May argue the case harder, refine the strategy further, or step back from the detail of execution.
DIC.coaching_adjustment: Translate strategy into specific commitments, check execution as closely as the plan, and hold owners to dates.
DIC.risk_response: Move from the plan to the next action, name the owner, and check progress on a set date.
coaching: Move from persuading supervisors about the strategy to coaching them through execution.
End every strategy conversation with owners, actions, and a follow-up date.
DIC.creates: credible strategic direction, persuasive influence, analytical depth, and confident decisions
DIC.development: carry that strategy into execution, so credibility turns into results the team owns
DIC.fly_risk: a compelling strategy can stall if execution is left to others without clear owners. Your Flywheel work is to ensure strategy is executed, not just endorsed.
DIC.fly_ground: strategic direction, persuasive influence, and analytical credibility
DIC.plan_60: Move from persuading about the plan to coaching its execution. Confirm owners and dates.
DIC.plan_90: Keep the strategic view while tracking delivery. Stay close to execution when the pace increases.
DIC.success: Your strategic credibility remains a strength, and staff increasingly turn direction into delivered results rather than waiting for you to drive each step.

quality: Strategic Clarity
You explain where the team is going and the reasoning behind it.
stretch: Execution Focus
You translate strategy into owners, actions, and dates.

DSC.natural_strengths: Results-focused drive and decisiveness, supported by steady follow-through, process discipline, and quality focus
DSC.experience: driven, dependable, thorough, and committed to delivering quality results
DSC.blind_spot: May focus so tightly on operational delivery that the bigger strategic picture goes unspoken.
DSC.pressure_risk: May tighten control of the process, take on more of the work, or become impatient with anything that slows delivery.
DSC.coaching_adjustment: Share the strategic reason behind the work, delegate process ownership, and lift your focus from delivery to direction.
DSC.risk_response: Step back from the process, explain the why, and let others own the delivery.
coaching: Move from running the operation to coaching supervisors to own it.
Ask supervisors to bring their process improvements to you before you step in.
DSC.creates: reliable operational delivery, process discipline, quality results, and steady drive
DSC.development: lift that operational excellence into strategic leadership that shapes where the team goes next
focus_move: coaching others to own the process
DSC.fly_risk: operational excellence can keep you in the process instead of shaping direction. Your Flywheel work is to ensure the operation runs through others while you lead where it is going.
DSC.fly_ground: results-driven operations, process discipline, and quality delivery
DSC.plan_60: Move from running the process to coaching others to own it. Explain the why first.
DSC.plan_90: Keep delivery strong while leading direction. Stay strategic and visible when operational pressure rises.
DSC.success: Your operational standards remain high, and staff increasingly own delivery and quality rather than depending on you to run the process.

quality: Reliable Delivery
You set a steady, quality-focused pace and keep commitments.
stretch: Strategic Voice
You explain where the work is heading and why it matters.

DSI.natural_strengths: Determined, results-focused drive, supported by steady persistence and people-present warmth
DSI.experience: determined, warm, persistent, and focused on getting results with people
DSI.blind_spot: May push the pace through personal persistence and assume the team shares the same urgency.
DSI.pressure_risk: May press harder on deadlines, take over when progress slows, or let warmth give way to impatience.
DSI.coaching_adjustment: Check that the team shares the goal, invite them to set the pace, and coach ownership instead of pushing harder.
DSI.risk_response: Check in before pushing, ask what is in the way, and let the team set the next step.
coaching: Move from pushing results through people to coaching them to own the result.
Ask supervisors what pace is realistic, then hold them to the pace they set.
DSI.creates: determined drive, persistent follow-through, people-present energy, and steady results
DSI.development: share that urgency with the team, so momentum is co-owned rather than pushed
focus_move: coaching others to own the pace
DSI.fly_risk: determined urgency can become pressure the team carries rather than momentum it owns. Your Flywheel work is to ensure the pace is co-owned, not just demanded.
DSI.fly_ground: determined drive, persistent follow-through, and people-present warmth
DSI.plan_60: Move from pushing the pace to coaching the team to own it. Ask before pressing.
DSI.plan_90: Keep your determination while protecting the team's energy. Stay warm and coaching-oriented when deadlines tighten.
DSI.success: Your determination remains a strength, and staff increasingly set and hold their own pace rather than relying on your push to reach the goal.

quality: Determination
You keep the team focused on the goal and moving toward it.
stretch: Shared Pace
You invite the team to set the pace and own the next step.

DCI.natural_strengths: Decisive, analytically rigorous direction, supported by persuasive, relationally present influence
DCI.experience: decisive, rigorous, persuasive, and able to engage people around a strategic challenge
DCI.blind_spot: May use persuasion and analysis to win the argument rather than to build shared ownership of the direction.
DCI.pressure_risk: May press the analytical case harder, persuade rather than listen, or move ahead before others have aligned.
DCI.coaching_adjustment: Invite challenge to your own thinking, build alignment before deciding, and let others shape how the direction is carried out.
DCI.risk_response: Pause the case, ask what others see, and agree the direction together.
coaching: Move from persuading supervisors to your view to coaching them to form their own.
Ask for their analysis first, then build the decision together.
DCI.creates: rigorous strategic direction, persuasive influence, decisive action, and analytical credibility
DCI.development: use that influence to build alignment, so people own the direction rather than simply accept it
focus_move: coaching others to shape the plan
DCI.fly_risk: a well-argued direction can win agreement without earning ownership. Your Flywheel work is to ensure direction is shared, not just persuaded.
DCI.fly_ground: rigorous strategic direction, persuasive influence, and decisive challenge
plan_focus: Coaching Others to Shape the Plan
DCI.plan_60: Move from persuading to coaching. Ask for their analysis before sharing yours.
DCI.plan_90: Keep your rigor while building alignment. Stay open and coaching-oriented when decisions are contested.
DCI.success: Your analytical rigor remains a strength, and staff increasingly shape and own the direction rather than simply accepting your case for it.

quality: Rigorous Direction
You set direction grounded in evidence and explain it clearly.
stretch: Alignment
You invite others' analysis before you decide.

DCS.natural_strengths: Decisive, results-focused direction, supported by analytical rigor, quality standards, and persistent focus
DCS.experience: focused, rigorous, persistent, and serious about quality results
DCS.blind_spot: May stay task- and quality-focused to the point that relationships and recognition are overlooked.
DCS.pressure_risk: May become more exacting, more closed, or more focused on the task than on the people doing it.
DCS.coaching_adjustment: Build relationships into how you lead, recognize effort as well as results, and explain decisions in human terms.
DCS.risk_response: Pause on the task, check in with the people, and explain the decision behind the pressure.
coaching: Move from directing the task to coaching the person doing it.
Open each coaching conversation with how they are doing before what they are doing.
DCS.creates: focused direction, rigorous quality standards, persistent follow-through, and reliable results
DCS.development: ground that focus in relationships, so people follow your direction because they trust it, not only because it is right
focus_move: coaching the people behind the work
DCS.fly_risk: a strong task focus can leave the team feeling managed rather than led. Your Flywheel work is to ensure people are engaged, not just directed.
DCS.fly_ground: focused direction, analytical rigor, and persistent quality standards
DCS.plan_60: Move from directing the task to coaching the person. Recognize effort before correcting.
DCS.plan_90: Keep your standards while strengthening connection. Stay relational and coaching-oriented when pressure rises.
DCS.success: Your focus and standards remain strengths, and staff increasingly feel engaged and recognized while they meet the quality you expect.

quality: Focus
You keep attention on the priority and the quality it requires.
stretch: Connection
You recognize the people doing the work, not only the result.

I.natural_strengths: Relational energy, engagement, optimism, and visible influence
I.blind_spot: May rely on relational energy and soften accountability to preserve harmony.
I.pressure_risk: May over-explain, become scattered, or avoid the direct conversation that accountability requires.
I.coaching_adjustment: Anchor enthusiasm in clear expectations, follow-through, and direct accountability language.
I.risk_response: Slow down, get specific, and have the direct conversation instead of smoothing it over.
coaching: Move from motivating to holding supervisors accountable for specific commitments.
End every coaching conversation with owner, action, and date, then follow up.
I.creates: energy, engagement, optimism, and strong relational influence
I.development: anchor that energy in clear expectations and visible follow-through
I.fly_risk: energy and enthusiasm can stand in for follow-through if commitments are not made explicit. Your Flywheel work is to ensure engagement becomes accountable execution, not just goodwill.
I.fly_ground: relational energy, engagement, and visible influence
I.plan_60: Move from energizing the team to holding them to clear commitments. Confirm owner, action, and date.
I.plan_90: Keep enthusiasm anchored in follow-through. Stay direct and specific when the pace increases.
I.success: Your energy remains a strength, and staff increasingly follow through on clear commitments rather than relying on your enthusiasm to carry momentum.

quality: Energy
You build enthusiasm and connection around shared goals.
stretch: Follow-Through
You turn ideas into clear owners, actions, and dates.

ID.natural_strengths: Relational energy, persuasion, and visible influence, supported by decisiveness and a drive for results
ID.experience: motivating, persuasive, confident, and able to energize people toward a result
ID.blind_spot: May rely on persuasion to move people and skip the structure that makes results repeatable.
ID.pressure_risk: May push persuasion harder, make quick promises, or move to the next goal before the last one is secured.
ID.coaching_adjustment: Back your influence with clear measures, confirm commitments in writing, and follow up before moving on.
ID.risk_response: Pause the pitch, confirm the commitment, and check it at an agreed time.
coaching: Move from motivating supervisors to holding them to measurable results.
Agree one measure per commitment and review it together.
ID.creates: motivating energy, persuasive influence, results focus, and fast engagement
ID.development: back that influence with measurable accountability, so results hold beyond the initial push
focus_move: coaching others to own the outcome
ID.fly_risk: persuasive energy can win commitments that are never measured. Your Flywheel work is to ensure momentum is tracked and owned, not just inspired.
ID.fly_ground: motivating energy, persuasive influence, and a drive for results
ID.plan_60: Move from persuading to measuring. Agree one clear measure for every commitment.
ID.plan_90: Keep your motivating energy while holding the measures. Stay specific when new goals compete for attention.
ID.success: Your motivating energy remains a strength, and staff increasingly deliver measurable results rather than relying on your persuasion to keep them moving.

quality: Motivation
You energize people toward a clear, ambitious goal.
stretch: Measurable Results
You agree how success will be measured and follow up on it.

IS.natural_strengths: Warm engagement, encouragement, and relational influence, supported by patience and dependable support
IS.experience: warm, encouraging, approachable, and genuinely invested in people
IS.blind_spot: May lead through care and encouragement while avoiding the standards conversation people also need.
IS.pressure_risk: May reassure rather than address the issue, take on others' stress, or delay feedback to protect the relationship.
IS.coaching_adjustment: Pair encouragement with a clear standard, name performance gaps kindly and directly, and follow up on what was agreed.
IS.risk_response: Name the gap kindly, state the standard, and agree the next step.
coaching: Move from supporting supervisors to developing them through clear standards.
Pair every word of encouragement with one specific expectation.
IS.creates: warm engagement, trust, encouragement, and a strong sense of belonging
IS.development: pair that care with clear standards, so people grow through expectations as well as support
IS.fly_risk: warm support can protect people from the standards that would help them grow. Your Flywheel work is to ensure care develops performance, not just comfort.
IS.fly_ground: warm engagement, encouragement, and a strong sense of belonging
IS.plan_60: Move from encouraging to developing. Name one clear expectation in every coaching conversation.
IS.plan_90: Keep your warmth while holding the standard. Stay direct and kind when feedback is hard.
IS.success: Your warmth remains a strength, and staff increasingly meet clear standards and grow through honest feedback rather than relying on encouragement alone.

quality: Encouragement
You build confidence and belonging in the people you lead.
stretch: Kind Candor
You name expectations and gaps kindly and directly.

IC.natural_strengths: Engaging, thoughtful influence and clear communication, supported by analytical judgment and quality consciousness
IC.experience: engaging, thoughtful, articulate, and careful about getting things right
IC.blind_spot: May stay in the role of consultant, offering thoughtful input without taking the decisive lead.
IC.pressure_risk: May gather more views, refine the message, or wait for consensus instead of making the call.
IC.coaching_adjustment: Move from advising to deciding, set a decision deadline, and communicate the call with confidence.
IC.risk_response: Set a decision deadline, make the call, and explain it with confidence.
coaching: Move from consulting with supervisors to leading them to a decision.
Close each coaching conversation with a clear decision and an owner.
IC.creates: thoughtful influence, clear communication, quality judgment, and engaged collaboration
IC.development: turn that thoughtful input into decisive leadership, so your insight shapes action as well as discussion
focus_move: coaching others to act on insight
IC.fly_risk: thoughtful consultation can slow decisions the team needs you to make. Your Flywheel work is to ensure insight becomes action, not just advice.
IC.fly_ground: thoughtful influence, clear communication, and quality judgment
IC.plan_60: Move from advising to deciding. Set a deadline for every open decision.
IC.plan_90: Keep your thoughtful judgment while acting with urgency. Stay decisive when the path is not fully certain.
IC.success: Your thoughtful judgment remains a strength, and staff increasingly see timely decisions from you and act on them rather than waiting for consensus.

quality: Thoughtful Influence
You communicate clearly and bring sound judgment to the conversation.
stretch: Timely Decisions
You make the call on time and explain it with confidence.

ISC.natural_strengths: Warm, reflective engagement, supported by steady loyalty and a careful eye for quality
ISC.experience: warm, reflective, steady, and thoughtful about both people and the work
ISC.blind_spot: May counsel and reflect with people rather than hold them to clear standards and outcomes.
ISC.pressure_risk: May listen longer, analyze the situation further, or protect the relationship instead of addressing performance.
ISC.coaching_adjustment: Move from listening to directing when it matters, set clear standards, and follow up on outcomes.
ISC.risk_response: Listen, then decide, state the standard, and follow up on the outcome.
coaching: Move from counseling supervisors to holding them to clear outcomes.
End each conversation with the standard, the owner, and the check-in date.
ISC.creates: trusted counsel, steady relationships, thoughtful reflection, and quality-conscious support
ISC.development: carry that counsel into accountability, so people grow through standards as well as support
ISC.fly_risk: trusted counsel can become a safe space that never asks for more. Your Flywheel work is to ensure support leads to growth, not just stability.
ISC.fly_ground: trusted counsel, steady relationships, and quality-conscious reflection
ISC.plan_60: Move from counseling to coaching outcomes. State the standard in every conversation.
ISC.plan_90: Keep your reflective care while holding people to outcomes. Stay clear and consistent when conversations get hard.
ISC.success: Your trusted counsel remains a strength, and staff increasingly grow through clear standards and accountability rather than support alone.

quality: Trusted Counsel
You listen well and help people think through what matters.
stretch: Clear Standards
You state the expectation and follow up on the outcome.

IDS.natural_strengths: Energizing, motivating influence, supported by decisiveness when needed and steady persistence
IDS.experience: energizing, upbeat, persistent, and ready to push for results when it counts
IDS.blind_spot: May keep the team energized and busy without defining what performance success looks like.
IDS.pressure_risk: May turn up the energy and urgency, spread effort across too many goals, or overlook quieter performance issues.
IDS.coaching_adjustment: Define performance outcomes clearly, track them visibly, and address underperformance as directly as you celebrate wins.
IDS.risk_response: Pick the one outcome that matters, measure it, and address the gap directly.
coaching: Move from energizing supervisors to coaching them toward defined performance outcomes.
Celebrate a win and name the next performance standard in the same conversation.
IDS.creates: energizing momentum, motivation, persistence, and a team that wants to win
IDS.development: direct that energy toward defined performance outcomes, so engagement turns into measurable team results
IDS.fly_risk: high energy can keep the team busy without defining what success looks like. Your Flywheel work is to ensure effort converts into results, not just activity.
IDS.fly_ground: energizing motivation, persistence, and a team that wants to win
IDS.plan_60: Move from energizing to measuring. Define one performance outcome for each priority.
IDS.plan_90: Keep the energy while tracking results. Stay direct about underperformance when the pace increases.
IDS.success: Your energy remains a strength, and staff increasingly deliver defined performance outcomes rather than relying on your enthusiasm to keep them busy.

quality: Energizing Drive
You lift the team's motivation and keep them moving.
stretch: Performance Focus
You define what success looks like and track it.

ISD.natural_strengths: Warm, motivating engagement, supported by steady, people-first support and decisiveness when needed
ISD.experience: warm, supportive, motivating, and focused on making people feel valued
ISD.blind_spot: May protect people's comfort at the expense of the accountability that would help them grow.
ISD.pressure_risk: May smooth over tension, take problems on yourself, or postpone difficult performance conversations.
ISD.coaching_adjustment: Treat accountability as a form of care, address performance early, and let people own their commitments.
ISD.risk_response: Name the concern early, frame it as care, and let the person own the fix.
coaching: Move from protecting supervisors to developing them through accountability.
Frame every performance conversation around the person's growth, then hold the commitment.
ISD.creates: people-first warmth, motivation, psychological safety, and strong loyalty
ISD.development: extend that care into accountability, so people are developed through standards as well as support
ISD.fly_risk: a people-first approach can shield the team from the accountability that builds momentum. Your Flywheel work is to ensure care includes standards, not just safety.
ISD.fly_ground: people-first warmth, motivation, and psychological safety
ISD.plan_60: Move from protecting to developing. Address one performance issue early each week.
ISD.plan_90: Keep your warmth while holding commitments. Stay steady and direct when conversations feel uncomfortable.
ISD.success: Your warmth remains a strength, and staff increasingly own their commitments and grow through accountability rather than relying on your support to carry them.

quality: Warmth
You make people feel valued and supported.
stretch: Candid Care
You address performance early as part of caring for people.

IDC.natural_strengths: Motivating, persuasive influence, supported by decisiveness and analytical credibility
IDC.experience: motivating, credible, decisive, and able to ground enthusiasm in evidence
IDC.blind_spot: May persuade effectively and decide quickly but leave the execution details and follow-through to others.
IDC.pressure_risk: May lean on persuasion and quick decisions, and skip the follow-up that makes the decision stick.
IDC.coaching_adjustment: Follow every decision with a clear plan, an owner, and a check-in, and use your analysis to track progress.
IDC.risk_response: Decide, then plan: name the owner, the measure, and the check-in.
coaching: Move from persuading supervisors to coaching them through follow-through.
Use the data to review progress with each supervisor on a set rhythm.
IDC.creates: credible motivation, confident decisions, persuasive influence, and evidence-based energy
IDC.development: follow that influence through to execution, so persuasive decisions become delivered results
IDC.fly_risk: persuasive, well-grounded decisions can lose momentum without disciplined follow-up. Your Flywheel work is to ensure decisions are executed, not just agreed.
IDC.fly_ground: credible motivation, confident decisions, and evidence-based influence
IDC.plan_60: Move from persuading to following up. Name an owner and a check-in for every decision.
IDC.plan_90: Keep your credible energy while tracking execution. Stay disciplined about follow-up when new ideas compete.
IDC.success: Your credible, motivating influence remains a strength, and staff increasingly carry decisions through to results rather than relying on your persuasion to keep them moving.

quality: Credible Motivation
You energize people with ideas grounded in evidence.
stretch: Follow-Up
You track decisions through to results with clear owners.

ICD.natural_strengths: Engaging, curious influence, supported by analytical precision and decisiveness when needed
ICD.experience: curious, engaging, precise, and willing to act on what the analysis shows

CDS.fly_ground: systematic discipline, analytical rigor, and persistent accountability
CDS.plan_60: Move from managing through systems to coaching personally. Add one personal conversation each week.
CDS.plan_90: Keep your systematic discipline while leading personally. Stay connected and urgent when performance slips.
CDS.success: Your systematic discipline remains a strength, and staff increasingly experience personal, urgent leadership from you alongside strong systems.

quality: Systematic Discipline
You build clear systems and hold a steady, measured standard.
stretch: Personal Connection
You coach people personally, not only through systems.

CSD.natural_strengths: Precision, structure, quality standards, and disciplined analysis, supported by steadiness, loyalty, patience, and dependable follow-through
CSD.experience: calm, thoughtful, prepared, fair, structured, and committed to getting the work right
CSD.blind_spot: May let the quality of the work speak for itself rather than making leadership perspective visible.
CSD.pressure_risk: May become more internal, more precise, slower to express concern, or more likely to carry the standard personally.
CSD.coaching_adjustment: Name expectations earlier, use concise language, ask ownership questions, and confirm follow-up.
CSD.risk_response: Pause, name the pattern, coach ownership, and confirm the follow-up.
coaching: Move from correcting or carrying to coaching supervisors into ownership.
Ask before solving and require the supervisor to identify the next step.
CSD.creates: reliability, thoughtful preparation, operational discipline, and strong quality control
CSD.development: make those strengths more visible and coach others into ownership rather than carrying the standard alone
CSD.fly_risk: strong personal execution can become a dependency if you don't coach others into ownership. Your Flywheel work is to ensure standards are transferred, not just protected.
CSD.fly_ground: operational precision, analytical discipline, and reliable follow-through
CSD.plan_60: Move from carrying the standard personally to coaching ownership. Ask before solving.
CSD.plan_90: Maintain consistency under pressure. Stay visible, direct, and coaching-oriented when the pace increases.
CSD.success: Your standards remain high, and staff are increasingly expected to own the work, apply feedback, and contribute to execution rather than depending on you to carry the quality burden.

quality: Precision
You clarify expectations, standards, timelines, and follow-up.
stretch: Confidence
You state what you see, why it matters, and what you recommend.

CIS.natural_strengths: Analytical depth and quality consciousness, supported by engaging communication and steady, patient support
CIS.experience: analytical, supportive, patient, and thoughtful with people
CIS.blind_spot: May support and analyze thoughtfully while hesitating to take the confident lead the team needs.
CIS.pressure_risk: May analyze further, support others through the difficulty, or avoid pushing for a decision.
CIS.coaching_adjustment: Take the lead deliberately, turn analysis into clear direction, and hold people to decisions with confidence.
CIS.risk_response: Take the lead, state the decision clearly, and hold people to it.
coaching: Move from supporting supervisors' thinking to leading them to decisions.
State your recommendation clearly, then coach them to act on it.
CIS.creates: thoughtful analysis, patient support, quality consciousness, and relational steadiness
CIS.development: step into confident leadership, so your analysis and support translate into decisive direction
CIS.fly_risk: supportive, careful analysis can leave the team without the confident lead it needs. Your Flywheel work is to ensure your insight directs action, not just informs it.
CIS.fly_ground: careful analysis, patient support, and quality consciousness
CIS.plan_60: Move from supporting to leading. State your recommendation clearly in every discussion.
CIS.plan_90: Keep your patient support while leading with confidence. Stay decisive when others hesitate.
CIS.success: Your thoughtful support remains a strength, and staff increasingly experience confident direction from you and act on clear decisions.

quality: Thoughtful Analysis
You bring careful analysis and patient support to the team.
stretch: Confident Lead
You state your recommendation clearly and hold people to decisions.

DISC.natural_strengths: Adaptability across styles, with access to decisiveness, engagement, steadiness, and precision as the moment requires
DISC.experience: adaptable, versatile, and able to meet people where they are
DISC.blind_spot: May adapt so readily that people are unsure what you consistently stand for.
DISC.pressure_risk: May shift approach with each situation, making your leadership harder to predict.
DISC.coaching_adjustment: Define a consistent leadership signature, and flex your style around it rather than instead of it.
DISC.risk_response: Return to your core approach, name what you stand for, and adapt from there.
coaching: Move from adapting to each supervisor to coaching them all toward consistent standards.
Name the standard that stays the same, whatever style the conversation needs.
DISC.creates: versatility, adaptability, broad capability, and the ability to connect with very different people
DISC.development: anchor that adaptability in a consistent signature, so people know what they can count on
DISC.fly_risk: wide adaptability can leave the team unsure which leader will show up. Your Flywheel work is to ensure your flexibility builds consistency, not confusion.
DISC.fly_ground: adaptability, versatility, and range across every leadership style
DISC.plan_60: Move from adapting to anchoring. Name the standard that stays the same in every conversation.
DISC.plan_90: Keep your range while leading consistently. Stay anchored in your signature when situations shift.
DISC.success: Your adaptability remains a strength, and staff increasingly experience a consistent leader they can predict and build around.

quality: Adaptability
You meet people and situations where they are.
stretch: Consistency
You hold a clear, consistent standard across situations.
